situation: Oumar travels by bus from Garoua to Ngaoundéré. When he leaves Garoua, it is 35°C. When he arrives in Ngaoundéré a few hours later, he needs a sweater in the evening.
Both towns are in the north of Cameroon, and Ngaoundéré is even closer to the Equator. Oumar does not understand why it is cooler there.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Oumar does not understand why Ngaoundéré is cooler than Garoua, although it is closer to the Equator.
What did Oumar need when he arrived in Ngaoundéré?
He needed a sweater in the evening, because it was cool.
What advice can you give to someone travelling from Garoua to Ngaoundéré?
He should carry warm clothes for the evenings, because Ngaoundéré is cooler.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand why temperatures differ from one place to another in Cameroon and in the world.

qa.q: Look at the diagram. Why are places near the Equator hotter than places near the poles?
qa.a: Near the Equator, the sun's rays are direct and concentrate heat on a small area. Near the poles, the rays are slanting and spread heat over a large area.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: Look at the graph. Why is Ngaoundéré (1,212 m) cooler than Garoua?
qa.a: Ngaoundéré is about 1,000 m higher than Garoua. Temperature falls by about 6.5°C per 1,000 m, so Ngaoundéré (22°C) is about 6°C cooler than Garoua (28°C).

sum.title: I. Latitude and Altitude
sum.intro: Temperature depends on many factors. The two main ones are latitude and altitude:
items: A. Latitude
Places near the Equator receive direct sun rays and are hot. Places near the poles receive slanting rays and are cold.
sun_rays_latitude.png
B. Altitude
Temperature falls by about 6.5°C for every 1,000 m of height. Ngaoundéré (22°C) is cooler than Garoua (28°C).
temp_altitude_cameroon.png

qa.q: Why is a cloudy day cooler than a clear day, but a cloudy night warmer than a clear night?
qa.a: By day, clouds reflect sunlight back to space. At night, they act like a blanket and keep the heat of the ground.

qa.q: In January, the Harmattan blows from the Sahara. How does it affect temperatures in Garoua?
qa.a: It is a dry air mass from the desert: days are hot and dusty, and nights are cool because the air is dry.

qa.q: Douala, by the sea, has a small temperature range, while Garoua, far inland, has a large range. Why?
qa.a: The sea heats and cools slowly, so it keeps coastal temperatures moderate. Places far from the sea heat and cool quickly (continentality).

qa.q: Why is it cooler under trees, and why are big cities hotter than villages?
qa.a: Trees give shade and release water vapour, which cools the air. Cities have concrete, zinc roofs, cars and machines, which store and give off heat.

sum.title: II. Other Factors of Temperature
sum.intro: Other factors that affect temperature are the following:
items: A. Cloud Cover
Clouds reflect sunlight by day, so cloudy days are cooler. At night, clouds keep heat, so cloudy nights are warmer.
B. Air Masses and Winds
Winds from hot areas raise temperatures, like the Harmattan from the Sahara. Winds from the sea cool the land.
C. Distance from the Sea and Ocean Currents
The sea moderates temperatures on coasts. Warm currents warm coasts, and cold currents, like the Benguela, cool them.
D. Vegetation
Forests give shade and release water vapour, so forested areas are cooler than bare ground.
E. Human Activities
Concrete, zinc roofs, cars and factories make cities warmer than the countryside (urban heat island).

evaluation: A town is 2,000 m higher than another. About how much cooler is it?
Why do coastal towns like Douala have a small temperature range?
The sea heats and cools slowly and moderates the temperatures of the coast.
Give two ways of reducing heat in a house in Garoua.
We can plant trees around the house and use thick walls or light-coloured roofs.
remediation: Distance from the Equator is called ______.
Height above sea level is called ______.
Temperature falls by about ______ °C per 1,000 m.
Clouds make nights ______ because they keep heat.
The effect of the sea on temperature is weaker far inland; this is called ______.
Cities are warmer than villages: this is the urban heat ______.
end.homework: Put a little water in a bowl in the sun in the morning. In the evening, check how much water is left and write where you think the missing water went.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 39: The Hydrological Cycle.
teacherNote: Data: Garoua 28.3°C, Maroua 27.9°C, Ngaoundéré 22.0°C (NOAA 1961–1990); Douala 27.0°C (WMO 1991–2020). Ngaoundéré lies at about 1,212 m.
Correction: Ngaoundéré is more than 1,000 m higher than Garoua (not only "a plateau"), which explains a difference of about 6°C.
